payload.title: Notice of Intended Marriage Explained Step by Step
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An engaged Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, planning a destination wedding, who have heard they need to lodge a Notice of Intended Marriage and want to know exactly what it is, when the window opens and closes, how to complete and witness it (including from overseas), which documents to bring, and whether it applies at all if they marry legally abroad, so they can sort the paperwork on time and get back to planning the celebration.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an advisor can plan the venue, travel, vendors and guest stays for the celebration abroad (the NOIM, documents and legal steps stay with the couple and their authorised celebrant).
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'notice of intended marriage' are mostly the bare government form page, state registry pages and individual celebrant blogs, and none speak to the couple whose wedding is happening overseas. This guide walks through the Australian NOIM step by step only as the Attorney-General's Department and the Marriage Act 1961 state it, dated once as at November 2026: what it is, the timing window, completing and witnessing it in Australia or overseas, giving it to the celebrant, documents and shortening of time. It then answers the destination question plainly: a legal wedding in Australia with the celebration abroad (NOIM applies), or marrying legally abroad instead (the NOIM is not used; a Certificate of No Impediment and local rules apply, stated only as official sources say and linked out), and recognition back home (linked out). Calm, exact and practical, with no legal advice.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: what the NOIM is and that it must be given to the authorised celebrant within the window the Attorney-General's Department states, dated 'as at November 2026', plus one line that couples marrying legally abroad follow the other country's rules instead. Then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways (what it is and who it goes to; the timing window as sourced; witnessing in Australia or overseas as sourced; destination couples: legal at home plus celebration abroad, or legal abroad with a CNI).

What the NOIM is and when you need it: the form, its legal basis in the Marriage Act 1961, and that it applies to marriages solemnised in Australia, only as AGD and the Act state it. Link /expert-advice/how-to-choose-a-wedding-celebrant.
The timing window: earliest and latest lodging times and how long the notice stays valid, exactly as AGD or the Act state, written in words with [[VERIFY]] markers until sourced.

Step by step (numbered): get the official form from AGD; complete it; have signatures witnessed by an eligible witness in Australia or an eligible witness overseas (only the witness categories AGD lists); give it to the authorised celebrant; provide the documents. No celebrant names. Link /expert-advice/what-does-a-celebrant-do-and-do-you-need-one-abroad.

Documents: evidence of date and place of birth, identity, and of any earlier marriage ending, plus translation requirements, exactly as AGD lists them; 'a fee may apply' only if a source says so, never an amount.

Lodging from overseas: how a couple living or travelling abroad completes and witnesses the NOIM and gets it to the celebrant, only as AGD states. Link /expert-advice/what-is-an-apostille-and-does-my-paperwork-need-one only if a source ties apostilles to NOIM documents; otherwise in the destination section.
Shortening of time: that a prescribed authority may shorten the notice period in limited circumstances, with the grounds only as AGD or the Act list them; no promise that it will be granted.

Destination couples (the differentiator): Option A, legal wedding in Australia (often small) then the celebration abroad, where the NOIM applies; Option B, marrying legally abroad, where the NOIM is not used and a Certificate of No Impediment and the destination's local rules apply (link /expert-advice/what-is-a-certificate-of-no-impediment-and-who-issues-it, /expert-advice/what-is-an-apostille-and-does-my-paperwork-need-one, /expert-advice/should-you-marry-legally-abroad-or-have-a-symbolic-ceremony); recognition back home in one or two lines, linking /expert-advice/do-you-have-to-register-an-overseas-marriage-at-home, /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate and /destination-weddings/is-marriage-in-italy-recognised-in-australia (draft; link only if live at publish). /destination-weddings/greek-orthodox-wedding (draft) only as an example of a religious ceremony abroad, if live at publish. This section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body (brand-facts claims only, venue, travel, vendors and guests, never paperwork) plus the /wonderland-concierge link (anchor names 'Wedded Concierge').

FAQ (4 to 6): What is a Notice of Intended Marriage? How far in advance do you lodge it? Can you sign it overseas? Who can witness it? Do you need a NOIM if you marry legally overseas? Can the one-month period be shortened? Each answer from the same sources as the body.

Close: the one Advisor line from brand-facts.md (never the definition line or its closing phrase). Links /wonderland-concierge (Wedded Concierge) and /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=notice-of-intended-marriage&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Any legal statement not from AGD, the Marriage Act 1961 or another official Australian government source read live; undated legal claims; legal advice ('check with your celebrant or the authorities' instead).
State or territory BDM detail beyond a link out, unless an official source makes it essential.
Any price, fee or amount; 'free'; 'a fee may apply' only where a source says so.
Rules for marrying in a specific foreign country beyond what an official source states; link out rather than restate.
Vendor or celebrant names; 'best' or ranking language; transfers, drive or flight times.
Anything implying the Wedded Advisor or Wedded Concierge helps with the NOIM, documents, witnessing, the CNI or legal paperwork.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the Advisor definition line and the phrase 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text.
Research talk in copy ('we could not confirm', 'according to our research'); per-line source credits; hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, celebrant blogs, directories or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images; reproducing the form itself as an image.
Clichés, exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
